name: Moderately-differentiated Thymic Neuroendocrine Carcinoma

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of neuroendocrine tumor with moderate differentiation in thymic tissue
Positive staining for neuroendocrine markers such as chromogranin A, synaptophysin, and CD56
Mediastinal mass localized to the thymus on CT or MRI
Symptoms consistent with mass effect or paraneoplastic syndromes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation with positive neuroendocrine immunohistochemistry markers in a thymic mass
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Differentiation grade is critical for prognosis and treatment planning

pathognomonic.symptomName: Anterior mediastinal mass detected on imaging
searchTerms: mass in front of chest detected by scan

pathognomonic.symptomName: Paraneoplastic Cushing syndrome due to ectopic ACTH secretion
pathognomonic.notes: May present with hypertension, hyperglycemia, and muscle weakness
searchTerms: excess cortisol due to tumor hormone

common.symptomName: Chest pain localized to the anterior thorax
common.notes: Due to tumor invasion or compression
searchTerms: chest pain in front of chest

common.notes: From airway compression or pleural effusion

searchTerms: unintentional weight loss and poor appetite

occasional.notes: Facial swelling, venous distension due to vascular compression

occasional.symptomName: Hoarseness due to recurrent laryngeal nerve involvement
occasional.notes: Voice changes secondary to nerve compression
searchTerms: hoarse voice due to nerve involvement

occasional.symptomName: Diarrhea secondary to vasoactive intestinal peptide secretion
occasional.notes: Rare functional syndrome associated with neuroendocrine tumors
searchTerms: watery diarrhea due to hormone tumor

occasional.notes: May be related to electrolyte disturbances or hormone secretion

rare.symptomName: Hyponatremia due to inappropriate ADH secretion
searchTerms: low blood sodium from excess ADH

laboratory: Elevated serum chromogranin A and neuron-specific enolase
Elevated ACTH levels in cases with ectopic Cushing syndrome
imaging: CT scan showing anterior mediastinal mass with possible local invasion
MRI to assess soft tissue involvement and vascular encasement
Octreotide scan or PET with 68Ga-DOTATATE for neuroendocrine tumor localization
genetic: No specific germline mutations identified; sporadic cases predominate
Rare association with MEN1 syndrome mutations
other: Histopathology demonstrating neuroendocrine differentiation with moderate mitotic activity
Immunohistochemistry positive for synaptophysin, chromogranin A, CD56

distinguishingFeatures: Lack of neuroendocrine markers on immunohistochemistry
Different histological appearance with epithelial cell predominance
Primary tumor located in lung parenchyma rather than thymus
Presence of germ cell tumor markers (AFP, beta-hCG)

redFlags: Signs of superior vena cava syndrome
New onset paraneoplastic endocrine syndromes (e.g., Cushing syndrome)
references: Travis WD, Brambilla E, Burke AP, Marx A, Nicholson AG. WHO Classification of Tumours of the Lung, Pleura, Thymus and Heart. 4th ed. IARC; 2015.
Filosso PL, Yao X, Ahmad U, et al. Thymic neuroendocrine tumors: a retrospective analysis of 160 patients. J Thorac Oncol. 2015;10(11):1723-1730.
Kondo K, Monden Y. Therapy for thymic epithelial tumors: a clinical study of 1,320 patients from Japan. Ann Thorac Surg. 2003;76(3):878-884.
